519 likes, 17 comments - nester.3d2a on June 7, 2026: "Here's a closer look at the OpenTerface Keymod and why it has quickly become one of my favorite accessories for Raspberry Pi and portable computing projects. 

The Keymod is a compact USB device that allows your smartphone to function as both a keyboard and touchpad for another device. Once connected, you simply launch the companion app on your phone and gain access to a full-featured virtual keyboard, touchpad, scrolling controls, and additional input functions—all from a single interface.

For anyone working with Raspberry Pi systems, cyberdecks, SDR projects, mini PCs, or other portable setups, the Keymod eliminates the need to carry around a separate keyboard and mouse. It dramatically simplifies mobile deployments while keeping everything compact and easy to manage.

The app itself is incredibly straightforward to use. It supports multiple keyboard layouts, allowing you to switch between Windows, macOS, and Linux-style keyboards depending on the system you're working with. The touchpad experience is responsive, complete with scrolling functionality and gesture support, making remote interaction feel natural and intuitive.

I've been using the Keymod extensively over the last few days, and it has quickly become a permanent part of my toolkit. The dual USB-A and USB-C design makes it compatible with a wide range of devices, and the convenience it adds to portable projects is hard to overstate.

What's even more exciting is that the team behind OpenTerface is actively developing new features and improvements that will further expand the device's capabilities. From what I've seen so far, there's a lot to look forward to.

If you're into Raspberry Pi projects, cyberdecks, embedded systems, or portable computing in general, the OpenTerface Keymod is definitely worth checking out. Be sure to show the team some support—they're building something genuinely useful for the maker and hacker community.  Video coming soon!!

94 likes, 15 comments - nester.3d2a on June 13, 2026: "This has quickly become my favorite mobile hacking and radio reconnaissance setup.

At the heart of the build is a Raspberry Pi 3B+ paired with the official 7-inch Raspberry Pi touchscreen, all housed in a custom 3D-printed carbon-fiber nylon enclosure designed to withstand the heat and abuse that comes with operating in the field. A roof-mounted GPS receiver and AccelTex antenna provide the positioning and RF performance needed for wireless surveying, signal analysis, and network reconnaissance while on the move.

The platform is built to be flexible. Whether I'm mapping wireless networks, tracking aircraft with ADS-B, exploring the RF spectrum with SDR applications, or monitoring local amateur radio activity, the system provides a capable and portable workstation that can go wherever the road leads. It serves as a compact command console for experimenting with wireless technologies, learning how radio systems operate, and observing the digital landscape around me.

To keep the footprint small, I'm using an Openterface keymod, which allows my smartphone to function as the keyboard, mouse, and control interface. This eliminates the need for extra peripherals while maintaining full control of the system from a device that's already in my pocket.

What I like most about this build is its simplicity. No bulky laptop. No unnecessary hardware. Just a compact field terminal designed for wireless exploration, radio monitoring, and hands-on experimentation. It's the kind of setup that can ride quietly in a vehicle, ready to be deployed whenever curiosity strikes.

At this point, the system is fully operational. The only things left are cleaning up the wiring and designing a permanent mounting solution to turn it from a prototype into a polished mobile operations platform.
